claim: The S42 allocation-fault scenario treats a run with `generic == 0` as `inconclusive`, never as a green pass, because no client-visible allocation fault or `QueryMemoryLimitExceeded` delta occurred.
S42 arms `memory_tracker_fault_probability` through driver URL parameters and pairs it with `max_untracked_memory=0` so small allocations reach the memory tracker.

The S42 consistency verdict separately reports post-restart equality, clean fsck `dangling`/`unaccounted`/`stale_edge` results, and the snapshot integrity oracle; `snapshot_oracle_checked == 0` is inconclusive rather than a pass.
A measured GC round reached 1830 seconds in `fold_ref_intake` while folding 404,065 logs, and one `pending_deletes` occurrence reached 77.2 seconds.
The measured ref-intake cost is `logs + 2 × edges` round trips at approximately 0.9 ms per trip, making the phase request-bound rather than CPU-bound.
In the measured intake, 7,565 edge reads were re-reads across 4,573 distinct manifests, or 39.6%; all observed re-reads were cross-transaction and none were intra-transaction.

For each ref log, GC performs one GET of the log body because the transaction must be read; for each edge it performs one HEAD and one GET of the manifest body because the reducer needs the blob list for both `-1` and `+1` edges.
The HEAD-before-GET pair is a standing-veto protocol step; its cost is measured as the number of edges multiplied by approximately 0.9 ms per round trip, without proposing removal.

The ref-intake loop is serial: approximately 1.9 million requests at 0.9 ms each imply about 1710 seconds, close to the observed 1830-second maximum and consistent with nearly all phase time being serial request latency.
Per-log GETs and per-edge manifest GETs are independent fetches; their application order matters, but fetching can be parallelized subject to the existing pool concurrency limit.
If the approximately 1710-second serial fetch floor were parallelized N-way, the ideal fetch component would be about 213.75 seconds at N=8 and 106.875 seconds at N=16, before merge cost.
Every added ca-soak counter must be registered in `utils/ca-soak/soak/signals.py` or the harness will not read it.

The CAS ref-chain design makes absence decidable through per-namespace contiguous ids, point reads, conditional writes, and an exact committed-through frontier; a pool-wide allocator that creates per-namespace gaps makes absence undecidable without a certificate.
Blob in-degree is pool-wide, so destructive GC rounds require a frontier proof for every catalog namespace rather than only namespaces returned by a listing.

A complete catalog GET is treated as an atomic object-version cut, whereas a paginated LIST stitches separately fetched pages and is not an atomic universe observation; downstream protocol can close staleness after a cut, but cannot recover a namespace omitted from the universe listing.

Within each `(namespace, epoch)`, durable ref ids are dense from 1 through the greatest applied sequence, and the next id is `greatest_applied.ref_sequence + 1`; the pool-wide `next_ref_sequence` allocator is removed.

Under the every-attempt rule, an id is freed only when nothing was sent or every sent attempt has its own conclusive rejection; a definite rejection after an ambiguous attempt keeps the namespace lane wedged.

A wedged ref lane stores its admission fence generation, and each later caller's flush performs at most one bounded same-key, same-bytes conditional create under that generation; there is no background deadline-resetting retry loop.

After any writer-epoch transition, the first touch CAS-walks the dead tail using the `slot-occupy` result states `Created`, `Occupied(bytes, token)`, and `Unresolved`; an occupied `EpochSeal` terminates the walk, while an occupied straggler is adopted and replayed.
An `EpochSeal` transaction contains exactly one seal operation; `prev_epoch_seal` is required on sequence 1 of every non-genesis epoch, including an empty epoch, and is forbidden elsewhere.

A missing intermediate epoch or a checkpoint frontier after an `EpochSeal` in the same numeric epoch is `CORRUPTED_DATA`; consumers must not shortcut a fold, recovery, `fsck`, or orphan sweep around it.

The ref catalog at `cas/ref_catalog` maps each logical namespace to `Creating`, `Live`, or `Removing` plus a random 128-bit `incarnation`; the incarnation is the opaque `life_id` carried by every life-owned stream and state key.
Namespace lifecycle transitions are `Creating → Live → Removing → absent`; there is no fourth state and no pruning finalizer.

A GC invocation performs a catalog-only pre-fold drain after acquiring its lease and before defer, stream enumeration, the fold catalog cut, folding, or successor-seal adoption; it deletes only complete observed `Removing` rows whose matching adopted life row has cleanup evidence and no durable hold.

The pre-fold drain takes a complete catalog snapshot, selects one eligible row, and restarts its complete scan after every CAS outcome; only a scan with no eligible row permits the invocation to continue.

Namespace removal deletes lifecycle metadata only; it has no `suppress_destructive` input and performs no physical deletion, leaving `_ckpt`, stream objects, `_files`, and other dead-life objects to the perpetual `cas/ns/` janitor.

The ref fold has one pure `buildRefWalkPlan(catalog_cut, inputs)` producer; it creates rows only for catalog `Live` or `Removing` entries, freezes the admitted key set and evidence, and supplies the same plan to DEFER, frontier, fold, and successor publication.

A fold seal has at most one ref-life row per `Live` or `Removing` catalog row in its cut; input rows whose opaque ids are absent from the cut are counted and dropped rather than admitted or used to force `DEFER`.

Runtime identity is scoped to `(life_id, admitted_fence_generation)`; a name slot is only a cache, and predecessor invalidation may detach only the matching runtime without clearing or rebinding a successor runtime.

`CatalogLifecycleReconciler` owns catalog lifecycle reconciliation and returns orthogonal `AuthorityStatus::{Authoritative,FencedOut}`, `CatalogResolution::{DrainComplete,ExactRowAbsent,ExactRowReplaced,ExactRowStillPresent}`, and exact `retired_lives`; unreadable resolution throws without producing a result.

The dead-life janitor enumerates `cas/ns/` separately from the fold's hot `cas/ns/stream/` LIST, takes one fresh catalog GET per page rather than per key, and deletes only after page-wide life revalidation and an exact fence/token check.

Janitor progress is stored in the leak-only `<prefix>/gc/maintenance_state` object registered as `FormatId::GcMaintenanceState = 25`; losing or repeating this cursor can repeat cleanup work or leak bytes, but cannot affect GC authority, frontier completeness, `DEFER`, catalog lifecycle, or successor publication.

Life-owned physical keys use the opaque-life layout `cas/ns/stream/<life_id>/_log/<txn>`, `cas/ns/stream/<life_id>/_snap/<txn>`, `cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_ckpt`, and `cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_files/<relative-name>`.

`_snap` remains under `stream/` because it is immutable and transaction-addressed, grouped with logs for recovery hints and covered-object cleanup; moving it to `state/` would require a second hot LIST or a simultaneous recovery-and-cleanup redesign.

An immutable catalog cut is the decoded bytes and object token from one successful `GET cas/ref_catalog`, plus a reverse index built once from those bytes; a consumer must not patch or mix that index with a later catalog GET.
Two current catalog rows sharing a `life_id` are `CORRUPTED_DATA`, not a first-row-wins condition; catalog mutation, REBUILD, decommission, fold adoption, and destructive GC fail closed on that cut.

A physical id returned by a completed LIST and absent from the corresponding later catalog cut is inert dead-life debris: the fold counts and drops it, while only the janitor may nominate its physical deletion.

After pool bootstrap, an absent or undecodable `cas/ref_catalog` is `CORRUPTED_DATA` and stops creation, removal, and GC; only bootstrap may create the empty catalog, and it may never be treated as virgin state again.

A server root owns live namespace work if and only if the mandatory catalog contains a `Creating`, `Live`, or `Removing` logical name under that root; opaque stream/state debris alone must not block owner or epoch recreation, and an unreadable catalog fails closed.

A same-name birth is refused with typed retry-later while its predecessor is `Removing`; the window includes the terminal fold and the next invocation's pre-fold drain, but no physical cleanup or pruning round.
The catalog remains bounded by `Creating + Live + Removing` entries under create/drop churn; stalled creators retain entries until fence-terminal reconciliation.

`cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_ckpt` stores `{life_epoch, committed_through | none, checkpoint_snapshot_id | none, last_epoch_seal | none}`; `committed_through` is the greatest transaction in durable acknowledged history, not the greatest key observed by a writer or LIST.

Checkpoint updates use one read-validate-merge-token-CAS algorithm for append, snapshot publication, and sealing; identical merged bodies skip the CAS, and a contribution above `committed_through` is corruption.

A checkpoint snapshot may never name an `EpochSeal`; before accepting a nonempty `checkpoint_snapshot_id`, every reader exact-reads the matching `_log` and rejects an `EpochSeal` before reading the same-id `_snap`.

The append order is immutable log PUT, `_ckpt.committed_through` CAS, in-memory install/acknowledge, and allocation of the next id; if the frontier publication is unresolved, the lane remains `NeedsRecovery` and returns no success.

Recovery never infers committed history from LIST or surviving objects; it exact-reads `_ckpt`, replays the finite arithmetic range through `committed_through`, and treats a missing required key at or below that frontier as corruption.

Snapshots are deletable only strictly below `_ckpt.checkpoint`; a stale pointer can only under-clean, and a missing sampled base requires rereading `_ckpt` to distinguish a concurrent advancement from corruption.

An opaque life id with no catalog entry is inert debris and never evidence of damage; the only exported catalog deletion transitions are exact-CAS cancellation of a complete terminal `Creating` row and exact-CAS deletion of a complete, unheld `Removing` row with cleanup evidence.

A terminal record unreadable before folding blocks legitimate removal in `Removing` and must be surfaced as a stuck terminal-corrupt removal; after the terminal has folded and cleanup evidence is durable, later physical inaccessibility is leak-only cleanup failure.

Life-owned readers carry `NamespaceLifeId{namespace, incarnation}` and a stale reader receives stale-or-`NotFound`; all ref and namespace-file prefix/key/cache helpers require the typed life id, while namespace-only overloads are deleted.

Creation uses catalog `Creating`, `_ckpt` create, and catalog `Live` conditional writes; publication from `Creating` is structurally impossible because only a `Live` life-minting resolution supplies a writer life.
Migration is recreate-only: pool format generations and backward floors advance together, old-format startup fails closed at pool open, and no dual reader or in-place converter is provided.

Same-name namespace reuse is a supported workflow for repeated `FREEZE ... WITH NAME`, explicit-UUID `ATTACH`/`CREATE` including replicated DDL replay, and engines whose table paths omit UUIDs; the incarnation makes all three safe.

Banning a database engine or restricting generation tokens to shadow paths was rejected because it would break supported same-name reuse and replicated-database recovery while leaving other rebirth routes unprotected.

Read-only and writer recovery perform no stream LIST for completeness: recovery starts from the exact checkpoint and replays exact keys arithmetically to the committed frontier; LIST is only GC/janitor discovery.

A writer-mount recovery that may have landed beyond the durable frontier exact-reads one deterministic successor; matching valid bytes permit the fenced checkpoint contribution, different bytes or an invalid successor are corruption, and absence permits the conditional retry.

After the mandatory pre-fold drain, the fold performs one strict `LIST(cas/ns/stream/)`, then one fresh full-catalog cut, and builds its sole ref plan from that cut plus the completed LIST observations.

Each catalog-admitted life is folded arithmetically from its adopted cursor through exact `_ckpt.committed_through`; an omitted life receives the same finite exact walk, while hint holes such as `0x1430c`/`0x1430d` are not correctness gaps.

A destructive round may perform condemnation, graduation, deletion, sweep deletes, or ref cleanup only after every `Live`/`Removing` catalog entry reaches its same-round `_ckpt.committed_through` frontier; missing checkpoints, incomplete walks, or budget exhaustion suppress all destruction.

The delete-site in-degree re-read is normative: a `+1` landing after a namespace probe but before condemnation can be protected by the existing `deleteExact` liveness re-check even when no rematerialization path runs.

A classification-4 `ShardCoverage` hold stores a bounded reason, offending position, and retry/backoff data per `(namespace, incarnation)`; `suppress_destructive = anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete` is recomputed before every destructive site.

Every carried hold is pool-wide suppression because blob in-degree is pool-wide; a hold retries its exact offending position and clears only after that position is folded and the result is adopted in `gc/state`.

With healthy authoritative `gc/state`, REBUILD carries all holds verbatim; with missing or undecodable `gc/state`, REBUILD has authority to reconstruct only, performs zero catalog deletions, and returns.
A manifest from epoch E is deletable only after the cursor consumes epoch E's seal and no unconsumed tail record above the cursor names it as a removal target; any uncertainty retains it.

Orphan-manifest deletion accounts for the manifest's exact blob/source edges through a separate accounting-neutral retirement input, consumes no ref-transaction ordinal, and does not require every affected blob to have zero total in-degree.

REBUILD reconstructs ref-life coverage and edges from the catalog, exact `_ckpt.committed_through`, and finite arithmetic tails, condemns nothing, and preserves holds; fsck uses the same catalog-authoritative universe and treats `chain-broken` as fatal in both summary and exit code.

The ref-chain design adds about two serial S3 round trips per committed chunk for `_ckpt`, one conditional PUT per touched namespace per epoch transition during recovery, and one catalog GET per fold round after the hot LIST.

Serial exact `GET N+1` until 404 was rejected because every probe costs a full S3 round trip, concurrent writing makes the stop unstable, and 404 proves object absence rather than acknowledged-history completeness.

Recovery from a complete stream LIST was rejected because completeness is the premise under test; recovery performs zero stream LIST calls and uses enumeration only for leak-only GC/janitor discovery.

The ref-chain design resurrects the project's I7 contiguity idea from 2026-07-10 and closes the documented `Late Predecessor PUT` limitation from rev.4 by spending the `_ckpt` GET/CAS pair required for bounded crash recovery.

The fence observability work covers both fence-loss modes: throwing renewal followed by self-remount (Mode 1) and silently hanging renewal followed by deadline expiry and late re-arm without remount (Mode 2).
Mode 1 observability uses `CasMountFenceArmed`, `CasSelfRemountCompleted`, and `CasSelfRemountMicroseconds`; Mode 2 uses `CasMountFenceExpired` and `CasMountFenceExpiredMicroseconds`.
Mode 1 timestamps the fence trip and remount completion with `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`; the duration excludes wall-clock changes from NTP steps and includes VM suspension.

The Mode 2 expiry detector runs at a durable-write admission refusal, not on the hot `mayMutate` read path; it atomically records the true `deadline_boot_ms` once per episode when `lost == false` and the deadline has passed.
Mode 2 outage duration is measured from the true expiry instant stored in `fence_expiry_reported_boot_ms` until `setMountDeadline` re-arms the fence, rather than from the first refused write.
Mode 1 and Mode 2 fence counters are disjoint: `tripMountLost` sets `lost = true`, while Mode 2 detection requires `lost == false`, so one fence window is counted as exactly one mode.

The classified renewal mismatch reason is retained by `MountLeaseKeeper` before `onRenewMismatch` throws, so `onRenewFailed` can emit it in the fence warning; the reasons include `same_epoch_state_uncertain`, `superseded`, `foreign_writer`, and `vanished`.

The added fence/remount log lines are edge-triggered once per fence episode and therefore do not need a rate limiter; if per-attempt failures later need throttling, `LogFrequencyLimiter` is preferred because it keys on logger name and format string, unlike logger-wide `LogSeriesLimiter`.
`write_grace_ms` is a disk-level `ContentAddressedSettings` setting with default `0`; zero disables the feature and preserves today's immediate write failure behavior.
`write_grace_ms` accepts any `UInt64` without additional validation; it flows from `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` through `PoolConfig::mountConfig()` into `MountConfig` and `CasMountRuntime`.

`CasMountRuntime::waitForWriteGrace` is a bounded, event-driven wait that returns immediately when `write_grace_ms == 0` or `mayMutate()` is true, and otherwise returns on fence re-arm, timeout, teardown, shutdown, or terminal lifecycle.
`waitForWriteGrace` never changes admission: after it returns, the caller must capture a fresh `fenceGeneration()` and run the unchanged fence check.

The write-grace wait uses a dedicated `write_grace_cv` and `write_grace_mutex`, never the remount, build, or ref-ledger locks; its predicate is `mayMutate() || remount_shutting_down || remountTerminal()`.

The grace condition variable is notified by `setMountDeadline` for Mode 2 re-arm, `armMountFence` for Mode 1 re-arm, teardown/shutdown transitions, and terminal transitions including `enterVanished`, `enterIdentityLost`, and `publishVanishedIntent`.

The plain-object write surface inserts `pool->waitForWriteGrace()` immediately before `admitted_generation = pool->fenceGeneration()`; the mid-operation generation checks in `CasPartWriteTxn.cpp:705` and `:747` remain immediate abort points.

The ref-log append surface waits before acquiring `ref_queue_mutex` or setting `leader_active`; placing the wait inside append-leader tenure would deadlock remount and shutdown drains that require every lane to be `!leader_active`.

When grace is enabled and a Mode 1 remount completes, the plain write captures the new fence generation; when Mode 2 re-arms via `setMountDeadline`, the generation remains unchanged and the write proceeds under the same valid incarnation.
Part B issues no object-store request and cannot make a fence live; only the unchanged self-remount or late renewal path can make `mayMutate()` true.
With `write_grace_ms == 0`, the extra wait call early-returns, generation capture and admission checks occur as before, and the observable write behavior is byte-identical to the pre-feature path.
The write-grace wait has a hard ceiling of `write_grace_ms` even if no remount or lifecycle signal arrives, and terminal or shutdown predicates unblock it promptly rather than waiting for the bound.

Write grace complements rather than replaces `CasWriteRetryLater`: after the bound expires or when disabled, plain writes still fail through error 668 and ref-log appends through `NETWORK_ERROR` 210, preserving retry-loop behavior for background writers.

The observed msan incident had a renewal PUT hang inside its retry loop, a silently expired `deadline_boot_ms`, and a later silent `setMountDeadline` re-arm without epoch bump or self-remount; this produced a roughly two-minute durable-write fence window with no transition logs.

The fence/remount design does not change lease TTL, fence arming, generation bumping, self-remount, claim semantics, or the fence-not-rescue behavior; it adds only logging/counters and an optional client-side wait.

The CAS merge-layout preparation is behaviour-preserving work to decompose complex algorithms, reseam tests, and produce review-sized pull requests; it does not land the feature or fix the cold-LIST and relink dangle-freedom gaps.
Upstream-affecting fixes are intended for both upstream ClickHouse and `altinity/antalya-26.6`, while the CAS feature itself is intended for `altinity/antalya-26.6` only.
Relative to merge base `4359a07f088`, the CAS branch was measured at 3060 commits, 1215 files, +486529/−163 lines, including 120 subsystem files and +44000 subsystem lines.
The CAS subsystem forms a dependency DAG `Primitives → Formats → Backend → Pool → {Parts, Gc} → Tools` with one `CasTypes.h → CasFormat.h` include cycle and no layer including top-level glue.

The feature is reachable through the single registration line `factory.registerMetadataStorageType("content_addressed", …)` in `MetadataStorageFactory.cpp:219`, enabling the subsystem to land dark until a small wiring change turns it on.
Complexity is concentrated in ten functions, including `Gc/CasGc.cpp::fold` at 1044 lines, `Tools/CasFsck.cpp::runFsckImpl` at 507 lines, and `Pool/CasRefLedger.cpp::flushRefBatch` at 570 lines.

`Pool/CasPool.cpp` is a 66-method facade mixing mount lifecycle, ref-ledger delegation, staging, plain objects, blob upload, metadata, and event dispatch; it is identified as the subsystem's god object and should remain a thin facade during decomposition.
The large CAS headers are not to be split: their comments occupy 53–61% of the files and document the protocols as normative reviewer-facing specifications.
The decomposition principle is to split decision logic from I/O and locking: pure functions operate on explicit state, while I/O and lock-holding remain in thin shells.
A pure unit may land with no consumer when it has exhaustive tests; this enables complex algorithms to arrive in independent reviewable pull requests.

Behaviour-preserving extraction is verified with the full CAS gtest gate and a soak run; a gtest-only gate is insufficient because lock discipline and ordering can fail only under production-like concurrency.

The upstream carve-out inventory includes `ReadBufferFromFileView` position corruption (B115), `ReadBufferFromS3` retry-cancel (B117), and `ThreadStatus` lifetime (B90) as standalone fixes with tests.
The target subsystem series lands in dependency order from `Primitives`/`Formats` through `Backend`, `Pool`, ref, writer, parts, GC, tools, and finally wiring; every unit PR changes no behaviour.
A test belongs in the pull request introducing the topmost unit it genuinely exercises; if a purported unit test needs five layers, the code seam is wrong or the test is actually an assembly test.
`src/Disks/tests/cas_test_helpers.h` is 1250 lines, included by 73 of approximately 101 test files, and pulls in five layers: `Primitives`, `Formats`, `Backend`, `Pool`, and `Gc`.
Splitting `cas_test_helpers.h` into per-layer fixtures is the highest-leverage test preparation and must precede splitting the largest CAS test files.
The completeness invariant for the produced series is that the diff between its tip and the refactored working branch, restricted to shipped paths, is empty.
The obvious CAS gtest filter `Cas*:CA*` under-selects entire families such as `RefWriter*` and `CaWiring*`; the release gate must enumerate test families explicitly.
The preparation plan keeps the existing 3060-commit history and does not rewrite it; it creates a fresh branch from `altinity/antalya-26.6` and adds one unit and its tests per commit/PR.
Only the curated `docs/superpowers/cas/01`–`11` set is intended to ship as documentation; the broader `docs/superpowers/` worklogs, models, and reports do not ship.

Stage A closes the LIST-incompleteness blocker for existing namespaces with per-namespace contiguous ids, in-band `EpochSeal`, `_ckpt`, arithmetic fold/recovery, a destructive-round frontier proof, and REBUILD-surviving holds; LIST is only a zero-trust hint.
Stage B owns catalog and incarnation work (`INV-3`), while Stage A remains functional using today's unqualified namespace key shape and discovery mechanisms.

Stage A hard-wires `frontier_incomplete = true` through `UniversePolicy::kDefault = StageA_Suppressed`, so `suppress_destructive` holds on every production round and all delete families remain inert until Stage B supplies the catalog universe.
Stage A's suppressed-destruction residuals include accumulating GC debris, pre-existing verbatim-file rebirth aliasing (R1), and manifest-less orphan blobs after condemn-nothing REBUILD (R4).

Stage A's `EpochSeal` grammar requires exactly one `EpochSeal` operation, requires `prev_epoch_seal` at sequence 1 when `writer_epoch > life_epoch`, and forbids it at genesis `{life_epoch, 1}` and elsewhere.

The `prev_epoch_seal` field is populated by recovery seals and by every ordinary sequence-1 transaction after an epoch transition; recovery installs the chain's final seal in `RefTableRuntime::last_epoch_seal`.

`slotOccupy` performs exactly one conditional create and, only on conflict resolution, one raw exact GET; it never lists, never retries internally, and returns `Created`, `Occupied` with occupant bytes/token, or `Unresolved`.
`slotOccupy` leaves byte comparison and operation adjudication to its caller; a conflict followed by a missing occupant is `Unresolved`, never fabricated `Created`.

`CasRefLedger::allocateRefTxnId` derives ids per namespace from `getGreatestApplied()`: `{E, greatest_applied.ref_sequence + 1}` in the same epoch, or `{E, 1}` after an epoch change; `next_ref_sequence` is deleted.
`CasRefProtocol.cpp:433` rejects any applied ref id that is not the successor of the greatest applied id with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, enforcing dense per-epoch streams on the read side.
The Stage A pool format writer generation and backward floor are bumped together; opening an old format fails closed with a message directing the operator to recreate the pool.
Pool recreation is refused while a live mount lease of any format generation exists; after the owner is terminalized, the recreated pool claims normally and a delayed old-writer write is fenced out.
`RefAppendWedge` carries `{key, bytes, RefTxnId id, uint64_t admitted_fence_generation}` and enforces at most one in-flight PUT per namespace lane.

`resolveWedgeOnce` performs at most one `slotOccupy` under the wedge's original admitted generation: `Created` or matching-byte `Occupied` adopts the operation, an occupied successor `EpochSeal` conclusively rejects it and clears the wedge, a foreign non-seal occupant is `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and `Unresolved` leaves the lane wedged.

Before a wedge retry acts on I/O results, it re-acquires the install lock, verifies the exact stored generation/transaction identity/bytes, and reruns `checkFenceOrThrow`; stale results perform no acknowledge, unwedge, or install.
The `_ckpt` value is represented by `RefCkpt{life_epoch, checkpoint_snapshot_id, last_epoch_seal}` and both append and snapshot writers use the same `mergeCkpt` semantic-max helper.

`publishCkpt` follows read, validate, merge, identical-body skip, and token-CAS; token conflicts retry only until the deadline, and every attempt reruns `checkFenceOrThrow(admitted_generation)` after its read and before its CAS.
Snapshots are deletable only strictly below `checkpoint_snapshot_id`; if a sampled checkpoint base is missing, a changed `_ckpt` token causes restart and an unchanged token causes `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

Recovery captures one `admitted_generation` and uses it for slot occupancy, `_ckpt` publication, and the final install-lock fence check; it must not install state after a fence bump during the I/O window.

Recovery's arithmetic tail exact-reads every successor key, including ids omitted by the hint; a 404 below a durable higher same-epoch id causes bounded restart and eventual `CORRUPTED_DATA`, never partial replay.

During recovery epoch transitions, `Created` closes an epoch, an occupied seal is adopted, an occupied non-seal straggler at `T+1` is applied and the seal is retried at the new `T+1`, and `Unresolved` enters transient retry; recovery never mints `T+2` blindly.
A self-remount cannot re-arm its fence while recovery is in flight: it cancels and joins recovery, or joins its completion, so no old-generation `_ckpt` CAS or install follows re-arm.

Fold arithmetic intake walks exact `expected = cursor + 1` keys rather than iterating `listing.logs`; a hint hole that GET finds is folded without anomaly, while a 404 with no higher witness marks the normal frontier.

Epochs are crossed only by consuming a seal at the expected id; an `EpochSeal` is counted as applied with `produced=false`, and a later-epoch record reachable before its seal is held rather than guessed across.
Per-namespace fold failures such as corrupt bodies clamp or hold that namespace, while the rest of the round continues; only a key unattributable to any namespace aborts the whole round.

`ShardCoverage` classification 4 requires `HoldReason`, `offending_position`, `retry_count`, and `next_retry_round`, and those fields are forbidden for other classifications; malformed hold grammar is `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

A hold clears only after folding through its `offending_position` and adopting the result in `gc/state`; if an above-cursor witness disappears while the gap remains, the hold changes to `WitnessDisappeared` and remains held.

The fold's `DestructiveGate` requires a frontier proof for every known namespace; a quiet namespace is probed with one exact GET of `expected_next(cursor)`, and budget exhaustion suppresses all destruction even if safe cursor progress is published.

`suppress_destructive` is true when anomalies exist, a hold is carried, or the frontier is incomplete, and it must be consulted at every destructive site including manifest deletion, generation prune, orphan sweep, handoff reclaim, and ref cleanup.

`UniversePolicy::AuthoritativeForTest` is passed explicitly only by tests with closed universes; the single production fold call uses `UniversePolicy::kDefault = StageA_Suppressed`, with no config, environment, or mutable-global override.

The temporal deletion closure has three normative arms: newly condemned blobs are not deleted in the same round, source-backed/tokened adoption rematerializes a fresh incarnation protected by token mismatch, and tokenless relink orders receiver `+1` durability before source-edge release.

The sweep's shared `manifestDeletionPremise` requires both consumption of the manifest's epoch seal and no unconsumed tail removal target; unreached frontier, budget exhaustion, or a hold retains the manifest.
REBUILD removes the old blobs-prefix condemnation path and condemns nothing; this deliberately leaves manifest-less orphan blobs unreclaimable until the separate build/upload registry work in R4.

Fsck walks arithmetic streams, reports physical objects above `_ckpt.checkpoint` as uncommitted debris, reserves `unchecked` for genuinely unproven cases, and returns clean for a healthy arithmetic pool.

Probe A is demoted from a fold-aborting hole detector to a sampled store-quality detector: it reports due/performed/skipped observations but aborts and gates nothing, while the round retains one strict hint enumeration.

The ref-layer `materialization_grace` wait is expected to be deleted because arithmetic recovery no longer trusts listings for completeness and the in-band seal fences late stragglers deterministically; the setting must not remain parsed but inert.
The LIST-liar regression backend hides named keys only from LIST while serving GET, HEAD, conditional PUT, CAS, and exact delete honestly, modeling the RustFS defect shape.

Under the Stage A default, a namespace absent from both the hint and `gc/state` can hold an acknowledged shared-blob `+1` while another namespace exposes a `-1`, yet the required result is zero deletes because `StageA_Suppressed` prevents data loss.

Stage A's soak PASS criteria require zero data loss, no wedge surviving a foreground flush or remount resolution opportunity, clean fsck, bounded `unaccounted` growth attributable to suppressed deletes, and no uninjected ERROR-severity log lines.

The initial arithmetic fold walk caused an unbounded-round liveness regression: concurrent appends made the walker chase the tail, producing zero completed GC rounds in 42 minutes on a hot approximately 30 GiB pool.

The bounded-walk fix freezes each round's work set at the round-start LIST tail: if `tail_listed > cursor`, exact-walk only through `tail_listed`; if equal, skip the namespace; if below, skip and count the stale listing, with no new persistent state.
The bounded fold walk adds `tails_advanced`, `tails_unchanged`, and `tails_below_cursor` phase metrics; an all-unchanged, hold-free round can skip per-namespace walks entirely.
A namespace reaching its frozen LIST tail is not counted as frontier-proven; quiet-namespace probes remain responsible for proving the frontier and detecting persistently hidden new records.

The bounded-walk follow-up measured approximately 444 logs per second as the concurrent writer/walker throughput boundary, motivating a stop-at-round-start-tail design independent of concurrent writes.

Fold-seal decoding rejects classifications outside `{0,1,2,4}` before narrowing, rejects classification-4 holds with zero `offending_position`, and rejects duplicate `(namespace, shard)` coverage rows; encoders reject the same malformed shapes.

Within one `putIfAbsentControlled` call, `DefiniteFailure` is reported only when every attempt is definite; any earlier unresolved ambiguous attempt dominates the call verdict and preserves `ApplyPending`.
